content: Pre-auricular cysts are congenital anomalies that are often connected to the external surface of the skin via a sinus tract. This tract typically opens into a small pit located just anterior to the root of the helix of the ear. In some cases, foul-smelling material may discharge from this pit. When a pre-auricular cyst becomes infected, it may require incision and drainage as an initial step. This approach minimizes the risk of recurrence. In pediatric cases, an infected pre-auricular cyst is often treated initially with antibiotics to manage the infection. Once the infection has resolved, surgical excision is performed at a later date to remove the cyst and associated sinus tract. During the surgical excision, the sinus tract and cyst are carefully outlined by injecting methylene blue dye into the pit. This technique helps to delineate the full extent of the tract and cyst, ensuring complete removal during the procedure.
